props.gloss_en: RSBG (mishna): one who buys [a nursing] animal from a gentile need not be concerned that perhaps [the young] was another's offspring
RSBG (mishna): one who enters his flock and sees first-bearers nursing and non-first-bearers nursing need not be concerned that one's young came to the other
the baraita's first tanna: the next born is a firstborn out of doubt, because [an animal] shows mercy even though it has not given birth
RSBG (baraita): the matter stands in its presumption
and so RSBG would say: one who entered his flock at night ... need not be concerned that one's young came to the other
(asked) RSBG means an animal is not merciful unless it has given birth -- so where it has given birth we are concerned it may show mercy [to another's young]
(asked) or perhaps: it is merciful to its own, but to one not its own it is not merciful
the practical difference: lashes under 'it and its offspring' -- if only its own, he is flogged; if another's too, he is not flogged
R' Yochanan: if one saw a pig trailing after a ewe, [the ewe] is exempt from the firstborn
and [the pig] is forbidden to eat 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you'

R' Yochanan: wherever RSBG taught in our mishna the halakha follows him, except for the guarantor, Tzaidan and the last proof
actually it is plain to him that the halakha follows RSBG, but he is in doubt whether RSBG holds that a mother that has given birth is merciful or is not
(would have been thought) even granting he holds a mother is merciful -- to its own kind; to another kind, not
he teaches the pig: it is merciful, even to one not of its kind, for one can say perhaps it shows mercy
Achai beribbi asked: one saw a pig trailing after a ewe -- what is [the law]?
(proposed) he asks about the firstborn, i.e. whether the halakha follows RSBG or the Rabbis
what he asks is: for the firstborn, according to the Rabbis; for eating, according to RSBG

questions.gloss_en: RSBG's 'the matter stands in its presumption': is a mother merciful [to another's young] once it has given birth, or only to its own? Three ta-shemas (24a.8, 24a.9, 24a.11) are deflected; no resolution and no teiku of its own
for the firstborn, even per the Rabbis who say it is merciful: merciful to its own kind only, or to another kind too? (closed by the תיקו of 24b.4)
for eating, even per RSBG: if he holds a mother is merciful -- to its own kind only, or to another kind too? teiku
